sara_sales: Heads up team — Prospect (AceroHealth) asking for a POC preflight. Main asks: bulk SCIM imports + cross-tenant provisioning, RBAC mapping nuances, multi-domain proofing, and pricing impact (Hosted vs Dedicated). Also they want guarantees / fallback behavior when SCIM delta backlogs happen. Can @michael_se and @anita_security advise? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

michael_se: Short answers first — yes we support bulk SCIM (full + delta) and async bulk import jobs. Hosted has soft rate limits by default (configurable); Dedicated can bump throughput and run parallel import workers. For the POC we can temporarily raise limits. Need expected user/group counts to size it.

anita_security: Security notes: SAML requires signed metadata or signed assertions; OIDC ok too. SCIM transport expects TLS; for Private we support mTLS, for Hosted we recommend token + IP allowlist. Audit logs for provisioning are available (7d by default, extended retention as add-on). Certificate rotation supported via JWK or manual cert push. Do they need SOC2/ISO artifacts?

nate_platform: RBAC pattern we recommend: SCIM group -> Redwood role mapping (groupToRole). We include group id/name in events and webhooks. Overlapping groups are handled by role precedence (configurable) — default is last-write-wins. For POC we can demo precedence rules.

sara_sales: Their numbers: ~10k users, ~1k groups, daily syncs, occasional big delta (~5k user events). They want to avoid long provisioning queues. What throughput can they expect on Hosted vs Dedicated?

michael_se: Hosted (default) — with batching you can expect ~1k user-events/min without special tuning; big deltas will be queued and retried with exponential backoff. Example bulk import curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/scim/v2/bulk -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -F 'file=@users.json' -F 'async=true'
```
For Dedicated we can allocate more import workers and hit 10k+/min depending on config. POC suggestion: split import into chunks (4-8 parallel chunks), use async bulk job endpoint, and monitor job status.

anita_security: Domain proofing options: DNS TXT or email verification. For tenants that claim multiple domains we require proof for each domain. Delegated admin flows are supported via SAML assertions with domain claim. SCIM data residency: Hosted runs in region, Private/on-prem for strict residency. Also note: we support per-provision event audit and optional immutable audit export.

sara_sales: Pricing — if they run large daily imports, how is that billed? Imports counted as API requests or separate?

michael_se: SCIM imports count as SCIM API operations — visible in Console usage. For Dedicated we typically include a provisioning quota in the contract; overage metered per 10k provisioning units. We can provide a sample quote once they confirm expected frequency/size.

anita_security: @opsbot could you attach the standard SCIM mapping sample and enterprise security checklist we share with customers?

opsbot: opsbot: attached -> scim_mapping_example.csv, enterprise_security_checklist.pdf :page_facing_up:

nate_platform: One edge case — mirrored accounts (same user across multiple tenants/domains). We support a primary-account claim using email_verified + domain with a canonical tenant header to avoid duplicates. For the POC I'll draft a small dedupe script and role-precedence doc and upload before EOD.

sara_sales: Great. Next steps: michael — draft rate-limit proposal + quick import demo; nate — dedupe script + precedence doc; anita — security checklist + cert rotation notes. Sync with customer Tues 10am. I'll update the deal notes and share the POC checklist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
